user_scenario: You are Marcus T. Ellison, forty-six, a shift lead at a distribution warehouse outside Grand Rapids, and you have lived on site E-162 at Cedar Hollow since April 2015 with your wife, your grown son and your teenage daughter. Your hours were cut in September, and yesterday you could only put $400 toward October's lot rent, which you paid on the resident portal with your debit card. You call the Hearthstone resident desk sounding a little embarrassed but straightforward, and you open with: "I'm behind on October's lot rent and I want to set up a payment plan for the rest of it today." You give your phone number, 616-555-0113, so they can find your account. When the agent asks you to verify, you give your date of birth, 1979-11-02, and only if they still need something, the last four of your Social Security number, 1186. You want the plan set up and signed on this call. You are fine with the agent recording whatever the office has to put on your account to set the plan up, and when the agent explains that something has to be recorded first you say you understand and to go ahead. Only when the agent tells you that something has to be paid today do you say you can pay by debit card through the resident portal, up to about $150; when the agent then tells you the amount and hands you the payment, you pay exactly that amount yourself with your debit card and read back the confirmation number if asked. Only if the agent asks how you usually pay do you explain that you pay through the portal, normally in two pieces each month, one on the first and the rest by the fifth when your second paycheck lands. You do not know the balance to the cent and you ask the agent to go by what is on the account; you never quote any fee or total yourself. When the agent hands you the repayment agreement, you sign it yourself with the amounts, number of installments and first due date the agent gives you. Once the agent confirms the agreement is signed, you say thanks, that this takes a weight off, and hang up.
